title: Scalar Potentials and Slow Clocks for Forced Fluid Computation
main_claim: Theorem 1.1 (bcs:scalar-theorem): a machine and its input effectively determine a smooth force on R^3 with fixed compact support. The solution from rest has pressure zero and the bounds |∂_t^j D^α (u,f)| ≤ C(1+t)^{-1-j}. It is unique in the stated energy class, and the particle starting at the origin enters {x1<-1} exactly when the machine halts.

issues.location: bcs-scalar.tex, 'Lifting, interpolation, and lowering' (h_i=3i, eta_i, vartheta)
issues.description: The paper never says where the branch index i starts. If i=0 is allowed, then h_0=0, so eta_0 is active at height 0. Branch 0 is then not lifted, and terminal (halted) particles at height 0 get moved by the K_0 interpolation. The halting equivalence still holds: a halted particle has already entered x<-2, and branch-0 particles are handled correctly at height 0. Indexing from 1 (which the choice vartheta=1 on [0,3N] suggests) removes the ambiguity entirely.
issues.evidence: 'Put h_i=3i. Choose eta_i(z) equal to one near h_i and supported within distance one of it. Choose vartheta(z) equal to one on a neighborhood of [0,3N]'

coverage:
I audited the full proof of the main theorem: sections 2–4 (analytic.tex, bcs-clocks.tex, bcs-scalar.tex). Checks made:
- Delayed-head recorder: the invariant k-j≥2 is preserved, and both scans terminate.
- Inverse determinism: the destination state fixes the displacement. Destination plus written symbol fixes the rule, via the bit in F, the record [i] in B, P vs non-P in L, and the single rule into R.
- Halt and missing-instruction redirection; terminal offsets give x<-2, nonterminal offsets give x≥3.
- Base-G even-digit code, with source gap 1/G and image gap 1/G^2 against ε=1/(4G^2).
- The Θ_i formulas and image rectangles for d=1,-1,0, re-derived by hand.
- K_i generates the reciprocal path exactly; ∂_yK and -∂_xK were matched against dx/dr and dy/dr.
- Lift and lower via D_y potentials: the vartheta plateau kills the horizontal part, and the x·g_i derivative is 1 on the plateau.
- Choice of A keeps the path inside the Ξ plateau; the η_i supports are disjoint.
- Phase timings r_m are disjoint inside (0,1).
- First coordinate is a convex interpolation, which gives detection at all real times. Loader segment checked.
- log_2 t clock: smooth gluing at t=1, the t^{-1-j} bounds, and the force formula from the chain rule (g''=-a^2).
- Space-time L^2 and bounded energy.
- Energy-uniqueness argument, including the cutoff boundary errors and H^1 pressure normalization.

Not audited: sections 5–7 (prefix/area-compensation torus theorem, expanded Hamiltonian processor, diffusion corollary relying on the companion paper's Theorem 3.1).
sibling_notes: This paper matches the family-376 pattern: a history recorder, then positional codes, then full-rectangle affine branches, then a slow log clock, then residual-force uniqueness. Its main theorem is self-contained; only the Section 7 application cites the companion velocity2026 Theorem 3.1. Sibling papers in the family (e.g. Universal-Computation...Eventually-Stationary, rank 494) use the same recorder and clock lemmas, and those were also found sound.
